assignedReviews.card_evidence: Objects can be grouped by their shape
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches grouping objects by shape, which has no connection to changes of state, particle arrangement, or energy changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Objects can be grouped by their shape
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about classifying objects by shape, not about melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Objects can be grouped by their shape
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address heat energy or any change of state process.

copy.en: Objects can be grouped by their shape, like putting all the round balls together and all the square boxes together.
copy.tl: Ang mga bagay ay maaaring pangkatin ayon sa kanilang hugis, tulad ng pagsasama-sama ng lahat ng bilog na bola at lahat ng parisukat na kahon.
copy.bis: Ang mga butang mahimong igrupo pinaagi sa ilang porma, sama sa pagtigom sa tanang lingin nga bola ug sa tanang kwadrado nga mga kahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: mechanical energy from your moving hand changes into sound energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes energy transformation from mechanical to sound energy when strumming a guitar. It has no relation to the water cycle or its role in the environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: mechanical energy from your moving hand changes into sound energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that water is one of the basic needs of plants and animals
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about energy transformation, not about water being a basic need of plants and animals. No instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: When you strum a guitar, mechanical energy from your moving hand changes into sound energy as the strings vibrate.
copy.tl: Kapag kinakalabit mo ang gitara, ang mechanical energy mula sa gumagalaw mong kamay ay nagiging sound energy habang nag-vibrate ang mga string.
copy.bis: Kon imong kusion ang gitara, ang mechanical energy gikan sa naglihok mong kamot mahimong sound energy samtang nag-vibrate ang mga string.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tiny glands beside each hair follicle make natural oil
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes oil glands in hair follicles, which is part of the integumentary system. G4-L-1 requires describing the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems. The card does not support any of these listed systems.

copy.en: Tiny glands beside each hair follicle make natural oil that coats your hair and scalp, keeping them from drying out and giving hair its shine.
copy.tl: May maliliit na glandula sa tabi ng bawat follicle ng buhok na gumagawa ng natural na langis, na nagbabalot sa buhok at anit para hindi matuyo at maging makinang ito.
copy.bis: Adunay gagmayng glandula tapad sa matag follicle sa buhok nga naghimo og natural nga lana, nga motabon sa buhok ug anit aron dili mauga ug mosinaw kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: reactivity generally decreases from top to bottom
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate plant and animal cells based on their organelles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the reactivity trend of halogens in Group 17, a chemistry topic. G7-L-4 requires differentiating plant and animal cells based on organelles, which is unrelated to halogen reactivity.

copy.en: In Group 17, the halogens, reactivity generally decreases from top to bottom: fluorine is extremely reactive and iodine much less so.
copy.tl: Sa Group 17, ang mga halogen, karaniwang bumababa ang reactivity mula itaas pababa: ang fluorine ay sobrang reactive at ang iodine ay hindi gaanong reactive.
copy.bis: Sa Group 17, ang mga halogen, ang reactivity kasagarang mous-os gikan sa taas paubos: ang fluorine hilabihan ka reactive ug ang iodine dili kaayo reactive.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: By handpicking! You manually sort them one by one according to their color.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: express quantitatively the amount of solute present in a given volume of solvent
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches handpicking as a method to separate buttons by color. G7-M-9 requires expressing quantitatively the amount of solute in a given volume of solvent (concentration). The card contains no solute, solvent, volume, or quantitative concentration content, so it does not support the competency.

copy.en:
How can you separate buttons of different colors?

By handpicking! You manually sort them one by one according to their color.
copy.tl:
Paano mo paghihiwalayin ang mga butones na iba-iba ang kulay?

Sa pamamagitan ng handpicking! Manu-mano mong pinagbubukod-bukod ang mga ito ayon sa kanilang kulay.
copy.bis:
Giunsa nimo pagbulagon ang mga butones nga lainlain ang kolor?

Pinaagi sa handpicking! Manu-mano nimo nga gibulag-bulag kini sumala sa ilang kolor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it also stops germs from spreading to babies and elderly people who have weaker defenses.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses handwashing and preventing germ spread, but does not teach that some organisms are unicellular (like bacteria) versus multicellular (like humans). No direct or prerequisite support for recognizing unicellular/multicellular organisms.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it also stops germs from spreading to babies and elderly people who have weaker defenses.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about hygiene and protecting vulnerable people from germs, not about identifying basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Washing your hands isn't just for you — it also stops germs from spreading to babies and elderly people who have weaker defenses.
copy.tl: Ang paghuhugas ng kamay ay hindi lang para sa sarili — pinipigilan din nito ang pagkalat ng germ sa mga sanggol at matatanda na mas mahina ang resistensya.
copy.bis: Ang paghugas sa kamot dili lang para sa kaugalingon — mapugngan usab niini ang pagkatap sa germ ngadto sa masuso ug tigulang nga mas huyang ang resistensya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Atherosclerosis makes arteries hard and narrow because fat deposits build up on the lining of the blood vessels.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a human circulatory system disease (atherosclerosis), which is unrelated to the competency about describing characteristics of the Sun. The tag is a clear subject mismatch.

copy.en: Atherosclerosis makes arteries hard and narrow because fat deposits build up on the lining of the blood vessels.
copy.tl: Ang atherosclerosis ay nagpapatigas at nagpapakipot ng mga arteries dahil sa mga fat deposits na namumuo sa lining ng mga ugat.
copy.bis: Ang atherosclerosis nagpatig-a ug nagpakipot sa mga arteries tungod sa mga fat deposits nga natigom sa lining sa mga ugat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Land, air, and water pollution are all ways that humans harm the environment
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes pollution harming the environment, which is unrelated to the competency about describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. No instructional support for mixtures.

copy.en: Land, air, and water pollution are all ways that humans harm the environment, making it harder for living things to survive.
copy.tl: Ang polusyon sa lupa, hangin, at tubig ay mga paraan kung paano sinisira ng mga tao ang environment, na nagpapahirap sa mga living things na mabuhay.
copy.bis: Ang polusyon sa yuta, hangin, ug tubig mao ang mga paagi kung giunsa pagdaot sa mga tao ang environment, nga nagpalisud sa mga living things nga mabuhi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The head of an animal holds the eyes, ears, mouth, and nose in place
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes animal anatomy (head holding sense organs), which is unrelated to techniques for separating mixtures such as decantation, filtering, or sieving.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The head of an animal holds the eyes, ears, mouth, and nose in place
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes animal anatomy, not changes of state of solids, liquids, and gases such as melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation.

copy.en: The head of an animal holds the eyes, ears, mouth, and nose in place, keeping them together for sensing the world.
copy.tl: Ang ulo ng isang hayop ang humahawak sa mga mata, tainga, bibig, at ilong sa kanilang lugar, para magkakasama sila sa pagdama sa mundo.
copy.bis: Ang ulo sa usa ka mananap maoy nagkupot sa mga mata, dalunggan, baba, ug ilong sa ilang nahimutangan, aron magkauban sila sa pagbati sa kalibutan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Can a polluted environment become healthy again?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses environmental recovery from pollution, which is unrelated to the solar system structure, celestial objects, or their composition required by G5-E-11.

copy.en:
Can a polluted environment become healthy again?

Yes! When pollutants are removed, the environment can recover. Plants and animals can return and live best in a healthy environment.
copy.tl:
Maaari bang maging malusog muli ang isang polluted na kapaligiran?

Oo! Kapag natanggal ang mga pollutant, maaaring gumaling ang kapaligiran. Maaaring bumalik ang mga halaman at hayop at mamuhay nang pinakamainam sa isang malusog na kapaligiran.
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang mobalik sa pagka-limpyo ang usa ka polluted nga lugar?

Oo! Kung makuha ang mga pollutant, maka-recover ang kinaiyahan. Makabalik ang mga tanom ug mananap ug mabuhi nga maayo sa usa ka himsog nga lugar.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Children need about nine to eleven hours of sleep each night
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses recommended sleep duration for children and its health benefits. It contains no information about particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects on particles, which is the subject of G7-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Children need about nine to eleven hours of sleep each night
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sleep and health, not about the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume. There is no instructional support for G5-M-3.

copy.en: Children need about nine to eleven hours of sleep each night to grow, learn, and stay healthy, so staying awake late is not good for the body.
copy.tl: Ang mga bata ay nangangailangan ng mga siyam hanggang labing-isang oras ng tulog bawat gabi para lumaki, matuto, at manatiling malusog, kaya hindi mabuti sa katawan ang pagpupuyat.
copy.bis: Ang mga bata nagkinahanglan ug mga siyam hangtod onse ka oras nga tulog kada gabii aron motubo, makakat-on, ug magpabiling himsog, busa dili maayo sa lawas ang pagpulaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heart failure means the heart cannot pump enough blood
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes heart failure, a medical condition about the heart's pumping ability, which is unrelated to the solar system, celestial objects, or their composition. The assigned competency G5-E-11 is about the general structure of the solar system, so this tag is incorrect.

copy.en: Heart failure means the heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs, causing shortness of breath and fatigue.
copy.tl: Ang heart failure ay nangangahulugang hindi kayang magbomba ng sapat na dugo ng puso para sa pangangailangan ng katawan, kaya nagdudulot ito ng hirap sa paghinga at pagkapagod.
copy.bis: Ang heart failure nagpasabot nga dili makabomba ug igong dugo ang kasingkasing alang sa panginahanglan sa lawas, mao nga magpahinabo kini ug kalisod sa pagginhawa ug kakapoy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heating materials can cause a chemical change
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of: a) number of parents involved, and b) similarities of offspring to parents
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that heating can cause a chemical change producing a new material. This is a chemistry concept and has no relation to differentiating sexual from asexual reproduction, which is the subject of G7-L-7.

copy.en: Heating materials can cause a chemical change, which means a new kind of material is produced.
copy.tl: Ang pag-init ng mga materyales ay maaaring magdulot ng chemical change, ibig sabihin may nabubuong bagong uri ng materyal.
copy.bis: Ang pag-init sa mga materyales makapahinabo ug chemical change, nagpasabot nga adunay bag-ong matang sa materyal nga maporma.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heat and work both contribute to the total internal energy of a system
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary resources to classify animals and plants of the Philippines as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses heat and work affecting internal energy, a physics/thermodynamics topic. G9-L-6 requires classifying Philippine animals and plants as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species. There is no connection to biodiversity or endangered species.

copy.en:
How do heat and work affect a system?

Heat and work both contribute to the total internal energy of a system - adding heat or doing work on it increases the energy!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakaapekto ang heat at work sa isang system?

Parehong nag-aambag ang heat at work sa kabuuang internal energy ng isang system - ang pagdaragdag ng heat o paggawa ng work dito ay nagpapataas ng energy!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pag-apekto sa heat ug work ang usa ka system?

Ang heat ug work parehong nag-amot sa kinatibuk-ang internal energy sa usa ka system - ang pagdugang og heat o paghimo og work nagpataas sa energy!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When coal, natural gas, and fuel oil are heated, they change into other products
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses heating fuels causing them to change into other products, which is a chemical change topic. It has no connection to gravity as a non-contact force or its predictable effects on materials and objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When coal, natural gas, and fuel oil are heated, they change into other products
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about heating fuels and their transformation into new materials, not about observing or describing the effects of gravity on the motion of an object. No instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: When coal, natural gas, and fuel oil are heated, they change into other products, which is why factories use heat to make new materials.
copy.tl: Kapag pinainit ang coal, natural gas, at fuel oil, nagbabago ang mga ito para maging ibang produkto, kaya ginagamit ng mga pabrika ang init para gumawa ng mga bagong materyales.
copy.bis: Kon initon ang coal, natural gas, ug fuel oil, mausab kini aron mahimong laing mga produkto, mao nga gigamit sa mga pabrika ang init aron mohimo og bag-ong mga materyales.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heating a solution generally allows more solute to dissolve.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the effect of heat on solubility, a chemistry concept. G6-L-7 requires describing living things as biotic factors and non-living things as abiotic factors in an ecosystem. The card provides no information about ecosystems, biotic/abiotic factors, or living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heating a solution generally allows more solute to dissolve.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe using labeled diagrams the biotic and abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs
assignedReviews.reason: G9-L-7 requires describing biotic and abiotic features of specific ecosystems using labeled diagrams. The card discusses solubility of a solute in a solution, which is unrelated to ecosystem features or labeled diagrams.

copy.en: Heating a solution generally allows more solute to dissolve.
copy.tl: Ang pag-init ng isang solution ay karaniwang nagpapahintulot ng mas maraming solute na matunaw.
copy.bis: Ang pag-init sa usa ka solution sa kinatibuk-an nagtugot sa mas daghan nga solute nga matunaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Exposure to extreme heat can cause animals to become ill and eventually die
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe procedures that the authorities have in place to alert communities of pending tsunamis and what procedures can be implemented should a tsunami impact a community
assignedReviews.reason: The competency concerns tsunami alert procedures and community response; the card discusses harm to animals from extreme heat, which is unrelated to tsunamis or any earth/space content.

copy.en: Exposure to extreme heat can cause animals to become ill and eventually die, especially if they have no shade or water.
copy.tl: Ang pagkakalantad sa matinding init ay maaaring magdulot ng sakit at kalaunan ay kamatayan sa mga hayop, lalo na kung wala silang lilim o tubig.
copy.bis: Ang pagkaladlad sa grabe nga init mahimong hinungdan sa sakit ug sa kadugayan kamatayon sa mga mananap, ilabi na kon wala silay landong o tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The heat of fusion is the amount of heat required to change a solid into its liquid state without changing its temperature.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines heat of fusion, a physics/chemistry concept about phase change. It has no connection to photosynthesis, respiration, or their raw materials and products.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The heat of fusion is the amount of heat required to change a solid into its liquid state without changing its temperature.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about heat of fusion, not the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work.

copy.en: The heat of fusion is the amount of heat required to change a solid into its liquid state without changing its temperature.
copy.tl: Ang heat of fusion ay ang dami ng init na kailangan upang baguhin ang isang solid patungo sa liquid state nito nang hindi binabago ang temperature nito.
copy.bis: Ang heat of fusion mao ang gidaghanon sa init nga gikinahanglan aron mabag-o ang usa ka solid ngadto sa liquid state nga dili mausab ang temperature.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heating a material makes its temperature go up, and cooling makes its temperature go down.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about temperature changes from heating and cooling. It provides no information about the role of solute and solvent in a solution, which is the required competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heating a material makes its temperature go up, and cooling makes its temperature go down.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses heating and cooling effects on temperature, not useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Heating a material makes its temperature go up, and cooling makes its temperature go down.
copy.tl: Kapag pinainit ang isang materyal, tumataas ang temperatura nito, at kapag pinalamig naman, bumababa ang temperatura.
copy.bis: Kung initan ang usa ka materyal, mosaka ang temperatura niini, ug kung pabugnawan, moubos ang temperatura.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it absorbs heat and changes from a solid to a liquid
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a solid (butter/lard) melting when heated, which is about heat energy and changes of state. G3-F-6 is specifically about sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, and its uses. The card contains no light content, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en: When butter or lard is heated near a flame, it absorbs heat and changes from a solid to a liquid.
copy.tl: Kapag ang butter o lard ay ininit malapit sa apoy, sumisipsip ito ng init at nagbabago mula solid patungong liquid.
copy.bis: Kung ang butter o lard initon duol sa siga, mosuyop kini ug init ug mausab gikan sa solid ngadto sa liquid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: place the container on a wire gauze to spread the heat evenly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a laboratory heating technique using wire gauze; it has no content about plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) or transport systems.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: place the container on a wire gauze to spread the heat evenly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about heating beakers/flasks with a burner, not about observing outer parts of plants or their roles in water/nutrient uptake.

copy.en: When heating liquids in a beaker or flask with a burner, place the container on a wire gauze to spread the heat evenly and reduce the risk of shattering.
copy.tl: Kapag nag-iinit ng mga likido sa beaker o flask gamit ang burner, ilagay ang lalagyan sa wire gauze upang pantay na maipamahagi ang init at mabawasan ang panganib ng pagbasag.
copy.bis: Kung magpainit og mga likido sa beaker o flask gamit ang burner, ibutang ang sudlanan sa wire gauze aron patas nga maapod-apod ang init ug mamenosan ang peligro sa pagkabuak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Which is heavier, a shoe or a slipper?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how different factors affect the solubility of a solute in a given solvent, such as heat
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about comparing the weight of objects (heavier/lighter), which is unrelated to solubility of a solute in a solvent. It does not support the competency.

copy.en:
Which is heavier, a shoe or a slipper?

A shoe is usually heavier than a slipper because it is made of more and thicker material!
copy.tl:
Alin ang mas mabigat, sapatos o tsinelas?

Ang sapatos ay kadalasang mas mabigat kaysa tsinelas dahil gawa ito sa mas marami at mas makapal na materyal!
copy.bis:
Hain ang mas bug-at, sapatos o tsinelas?

Ang sapatos kasagarang mas bug-at kaysa tsinelas tungod kay gihimo kini sa mas daghan ug mas baga nga materyal!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can give donations or be a volunteer in relief operations
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses helping typhoon victims through donations and volunteering. It contains no content about changes of state of solids, liquids, and gases, nor diagrams or flowcharts. The competency is entirely unrelated to the card.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can give donations or be a volunteer in relief operations
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about typhoon relief efforts, not about how temperature changes cause matter to change state. No instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can give donations or be a volunteer in relief operations
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address particle arrangement, energy changes, or state changes. It is about humanitarian aid after a typhoon, so it is unrelated to this matter competency.

copy.en:
How can you help victims of a typhoon?

You can give donations or be a volunteer in relief operations to help people who lost their homes!
copy.tl:
Paano ka makakatulong sa mga biktima ng bagyo?

Maaari kang magbigay ng donasyon o maging volunteer sa relief operations para tulungan ang mga nawalan ng tahanan!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nimo pagtabang sa mga biktima sa bagyo?

Makahatag ka og donasyon o mahimong volunteer sa relief operations aron tabangan ang mga nawad-an og balay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Herbal cream is a medicine made from herbs that is applied to the skin to treat health issues.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a physical model or use drawings to demonstrate how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit around the Sun affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas of Earth over a year
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses herbal medicine applied to the skin, which has no relation to Earth's tilt, sunlight intensity, or orbital mechanics. It does not support any part of the competency.

copy.en:
Can herbs be used as medicine?

Yes! Herbal cream is a medicine made from herbs that is applied to the skin to treat health issues.
copy.tl:
Maaari bang gamiting gamot ang mga halamang-gamot?

Oo! Ang herbal cream ay gamot na gawa sa mga halamang-gamot na ipinapahid sa balat para gamutin ang mga problema sa kalusugan.
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang gamiton nga tambal ang mga hilba?

Oo! Ang herbal cream usa ka tambal nga gihimo gikan sa mga hilba nga ipahid sa panit aron matambal ang mga problema sa panglawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hexyne is an organic compound
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the structure of hexyne (an alkyne with a triple bond). It does not address particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects on particles, which are the focus of G7-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hexyne is an organic compound
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about an organic chemical structure, not about how sound is made or transferred. It has no connection to the G3-F-4 competency.

copy.en: Hexyne is an organic compound with a chain of six carbon atoms that contains a triple bond between two of the carbons.
copy.tl: Ang hexyne ay isang organic compound na may chain ng anim na carbon atoms na naglalaman ng triple bond sa pagitan ng dalawa sa mga carbon.
copy.bis: Ang hexyne usa ka organic compound nga adunay chain sa unom ka carbon atoms nga adunay triple bond tali sa duha sa mga carbon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An air conditioner has a high power rating, so every extra hour adds a big amount of kilowatt-hours to the bill!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses electrical power consumption (kilowatt-hours) of an appliance, not electromagnetic waves, wavelengths, or frequencies. No support for comparing EM wave types.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An air conditioner has a high power rating, so every extra hour adds a big amount of kilowatt-hours to the bill!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about electrical power rating and energy usage, not about conduction, convection, or radiation. It does not identify advantageous or disadvantageous examples of heat transfer.

copy.en:
Why does our bill go up so much when we use the air conditioner longer?

An air conditioner has a high power rating, so every extra hour adds a big amount of kilowatt-hours to the bill!
copy.tl:
Bakit tumataas nang husto ang bill natin kapag mas matagal nating ginagamit ang air conditioner?

May mataas na power rating ang air conditioner, kaya bawat dagdag na oras ay nagdadagdag ng malaking kilowatt-hour sa bill!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga motaas pag-ayo ang atong bill kon mas dugay nato gamiton ang air conditioner?

Ang air conditioner adunay taas nga power rating, mao nga ang matag dugang nga oras makadugang ug daghang kilowatt-hour sa bill!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Launching a projectile from a higher place, like a table, gives it more time to fall, so it travels a longer range before landing.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes projectile motion and launch height, which is a physics concept. G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system, celestial objects, and their features/composition. The card provides no information about the solar system and is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Launching a projectile from a higher place, like a table, gives it more time to fall, so it travels a longer range before landing.
copy.tl: Kapag inilunsad ang projectile mula sa mas mataas na lugar, tulad ng mesa, mas mahaba ang oras nito para bumagsak, kaya mas malayo ang mararating nito bago lumapag.
copy.bis: Kung ilunsad ang projectile gikan sa mas taas nga lugar, sama sa lamesa, mas taas ang oras nga mahulog kini, mao nga mas layo ang maabot sa dili pa motugpa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The fossil record is like a stack of old photographs, giving a chronological record of the history of life on Earth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how increased societal uses of renewable energies could mitigate the effects of global climate change, including how the Philippines could make better use of its plentiful natural resources
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the fossil record and history of life, which is unrelated to the competency about increased societal uses of renewable energies mitigating climate change and the Philippines' natural resources.

copy.en: The fossil record is like a stack of old photographs, giving a chronological record of the history of life on Earth.
copy.tl: Ang fossil record ay parang salansan ng mga lumang litrato, nagbibigay ng chronological record ng kasaysayan ng buhay sa Earth.
copy.bis: Ang fossil record sama sa usa ka pundok sa daan nga mga litrato, naghatag ug chronological record sa kasaysayan sa kinabuhi sa Earth.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: honeycomb cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the geometric efficiency of hexagon-shaped honeycomb cells (space-filling, minimal wax). It does not describe any animal outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in movement or food gathering.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: hexagons fill space with no gaps
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the shape efficiency of honeycomb cells, not the physical properties of solid materials (hard, shiny, stretchable). No solid material property is described.

copy.en:
Why are honeycomb cells shaped like hexagons?

Because it's the most efficient shape — hexagons fill space with no gaps and use the least amount of wax.
copy.tl:
Bakit hexagon ang hugis ng pugad ng bubuyog?

Dahil ito ang pinakamatipid na hugis — punung-puno ito nang walang sayang na puwang at kaunti lang ang pagkit na kailangan.
copy.bis:
Nganong hexagon ang porma sa salag sa putyukan?

Kay kini ang labing tipid nga porma — mapuno kini nga walay luwang ug gamay ra ang gikinahanglan nga talo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Grasshoppers, frogs, and kangaroos hop or jump using their strong hind legs.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how fossils can be used for dating the age of rocks and sediments
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how certain animals move by hopping using hind legs. It contains no information about fossils, rock/sediment dating, or geologic time, which are the subjects of G9-E-4. The tag is unrelated to the card content.

copy.en: Grasshoppers, frogs, and kangaroos hop or jump using their strong hind legs.
copy.tl: Ang mga tipaklong, palaka, at kangaroo ay lumulukso o tumatalon gamit ang kanilang malalakas na hulihang binti.
copy.bis: Ang mga apan, baki, ug kangaroo molukso o motingkagol gamit ang ilang kusgan nga pangulahing mga tiil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The equator receives direct solar rays all year round, producing a hot climate with little seasonal change.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that chemical equations demonstrate a rearrangement of atoms but the total mass of the system remains the same during a chemical reaction
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses equatorial climate and solar radiation, with no mention of chemical equations, rearrangement of atoms, or conservation of mass. It does not support the competency in any way.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The equator receives direct solar rays all year round, producing a hot climate with little seasonal change.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about climate and solar rays, not chemical changes, bond formation/breaking, or new substances. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: The equator receives direct solar rays all year round, producing a hot climate with little seasonal change.
copy.tl: Ang equator ay tumatanggap ng direktang solar rays sa buong taon, kaya mainit ang klima nito na may kaunting pagbabago sa panahon.
copy.bis: Ang equator makadawat ug direktang solar rays sa tibuok tuig, mao nga init ang klima niini nga adunay gamay nga kausaban sa panahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It can be extremely hot, reaching 350°C or higher at the top, even though the air is very thin!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the temperature of the thermosphere, not the reflection or refraction of light using mirrors, lenses, or prisms. No instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It can be extremely hot, reaching 350°C or higher at the top, even though the air is very thin!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about thermosphere temperature, not sources of light, how light behaves, or its uses. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Is the thermosphere hot or cold?

It can be extremely hot, reaching 350°C or higher at the top, even though the air is very thin!
copy.tl:
Mainit ba o malamig ang thermosphere?

Maaari itong maging sobrang init, umaabot sa 350°C o mas mataas pa sa itaas, kahit na napakanipis ng hangin!
copy.bis:
Init ba o bugnaw ang thermosphere?

Mahimo kining hilabihan ka init, moabot sa 350°C o mas taas pa sa taas, bisan pa nga nipis kaayo ang hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A pulley uses grooved wheels and ropes or chains to raise, lower, or move a load.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how a pulley (a simple machine) works. G8-L-2 requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion. The card contains no information about body systems or their interactions, so it does not support this competency at all.

copy.en: A pulley uses grooved wheels and ropes or chains to raise, lower, or move a load.
copy.tl: Ang pulley ay gumagamit ng mga grooved wheels at lubid o kadena upang itaas, ibaba, o ilipat ang isang load.
copy.bis: Ang pulley naggamit og mga grooved wheels ug pisi o kadena aron ipataas, ipaubos, o ibalhin ang usa ka load.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Firefighters extinguish fires
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify solutions, which can be found at home and in school and that react with litmus indicator, as acids, bases, and salts
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses firefighting methods (cooling and fuel removal) and contains no content about solutions, litmus indicators, acids, bases, or salts. It does not support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Firefighters extinguish fires
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify common acids, bases, and salts (e.g., hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, and saline solution) using different indicators
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about fire suppression, not about identifying acids, bases, or salts using indicators. No relevant instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: Firefighters extinguish fires by cooling surfaces with water to reduce heat or by removing the fuel source, trapping the fire's spread.
copy.tl: Pinapatay ng mga bumbero ang apoy sa pamamagitan ng pagpapalamig sa mga surface gamit ang tubig para mabawasan ang init o sa pag-alis ng pinagmumulan ng fuel, kaya napipigilan ang pagkalat ng apoy.
copy.bis: Ang mga bombero nagpalong sa kalayo pinaagi sa pagpabugnaw sa mga surface gamit ang tubig aron mamenosan ang kainit o pinaagi sa pagkuha sa gigikanan sa fuel, mao nga napugngan ang pagkaylap sa kalayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soil is arranged in layers or horizons during its formation
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes soil layers/horizons and their identification by color and particle size. G5-E-12 requires making drawings or a model of Earth-Moon-Sun motion to explain moon phases. There is no connection to astronomy, moon phases, or Earth-Moon-Sun motion.

copy.en: Soil is arranged in layers or horizons during its formation, and these layers can be identified by their color and particle size.
copy.tl: Ang lupa ay nakaayos sa mga patong o horizons habang ito ay nabubuo, at ang mga patong na ito ay makikilala sa kanilang kulay at laki ng particle.
copy.bis: Ang yuta gihan-ay sa mga patong o horizons samtang kini naporma, ug kining mga patong mailhan pinaagi sa ilang kolor ug gidak-on sa particle.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What do humans get from high biodiversity?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses benefits of biodiversity (food, medicines, materials), which is a life science/ecology topic. G8-M-4 is about properties of pure substances, elements, and compounds. No instructional support for that competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What do humans get from high biodiversity?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical names of some common ionic compounds, including sodium chloride (NaCl), magnesium oxide (MgO), potassium chloride (KCl) and magnesium chloride (MgCl2)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about biodiversity benefits, not about writing chemical formulas of ionic compounds. No connection to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What do humans get from high biodiversity?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical name of some common covalent compounds, including water (H2O), carbon dioxide (CO2), and ammonia (NH3)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about biodiversity benefits, not about covalent compound formulas. No instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
What do humans get from high biodiversity?

We get more food, meat, fruits, medicines, fibers, paper, marine and forest products, wood, and building materials!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nakukuha ng tao mula sa high biodiversity?

Nakakakuha tayo ng mas maraming pagkain, karne, prutas, gamot, fibers, papel, produktong pandagat at pangkagubatan, kahoy, at mga materyales sa pagtatayo!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang makuha sa mga tawo gikan sa high biodiversity?

Makakuha kita og mas daghang pagkaon, karne, prutas, tambal, fibers, papel, produkto sa dagat ug kalasangan, kahoy, ug mga materyales sa pagtukod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: break rocks into smaller pieces
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about making objects move (pushing, pulling, rolling, carrying, or natural causes like wind and water). The card describes breaking rocks through mining, quarrying, and construction, which is about breaking or fragmenting rocks, not moving objects. It does not support the stated skill.

copy.en: Human activities such as mining, quarrying, and construction break rocks into smaller pieces.
copy.tl: Ang mga gawain ng tao tulad ng mining, quarrying, at construction ay nagbabasag ng mga bato sa mas maliliit na piraso.
copy.bis: Ang mga kalihokan sa tawo sama sa mining, quarrying, ug construction nagabuak sa mga bato ngadto sa gagmayng mga piraso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Humans are classified step by step as Domain Eukarya, Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Primates, Family Hominidae, Genus Homo, and Species sapiens.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the taxonomic classification of humans. It has no content about earthquakes, their magnitude, or effects on communities, which is the subject of G7-E-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Humans are classified step by step as Domain Eukarya, Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Primates, Family Hominidae, Genus Homo, and Species sapiens.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make models of fault scenarios to illustrate: a. the epicenter of an earthquake from its focus, b. the intensity of an earthquake from its magnitude, and c. how underwater earthquakes may or may not generate tsunamis
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about human taxonomy and does not address fault models, epicenter, focus, intensity, magnitude, or tsunamis, which are the required topics of G7-E-5.

copy.en: Humans are classified step by step as Domain Eukarya, Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Primates, Family Hominidae, Genus Homo, and Species sapiens.
copy.tl: Ang tao ay inuuri nang hakbang-hakbang bilang Domain Eukarya, Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Primates, Family Hominidae, Genus Homo, at Species sapiens.
copy.bis: Ang tao kay giklasipika sa matag lakang isip Domain Eukarya, Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Order Primates, Family Hominidae, Genus Homo, ug Species sapiens.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The upper arm has one long bone called the humerus, while the lower arm has two bones: the radius and the ulna.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the names and locations of arm bones (humerus, radius, ulna). The competency G3-M-5 requires describing physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card does not address any physical properties of materials; it is about human anatomy, which is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: The upper arm has one long bone called the humerus, while the lower arm has two bones: the radius and the ulna.
copy.tl: Ang upper arm ay may isang mahabang buto na tinatawag na humerus, habang ang lower arm ay may dalawang buto: ang radius at ulna.
copy.bis: Ang upper arm adunay usa ka taas nga bukog nga gitawag ug humerus, samtang ang lower arm adunay duha ka bukog: ang radius ug ulna.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Human activities like hunting too many animals can break a food chain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about ecology (food chains) and has no relation to assembling or drawing simple circuits. The competency requires building/drawing a circuit with batteries, wires, switch, and bulb/motor/buzzer, which is entirely absent.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Human activities like hunting too many animals can break a food chain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw diagrams of and assemble series and parallel circuits, showing switch, battery, loads/resistors, ammeter, and voltmeter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses hunting and food chains, not series/parallel circuits, switches, batteries, loads, ammeter, or voltmeter. No instructional support for this physics competency.

copy.en: Human activities like hunting too many animals can break a food chain, leaving predators without enough food.
copy.tl: Ang mga gawain ng tao tulad ng labis na pangangaso ng mga hayop ay maaaring makasira sa isang food chain, na nag-iiwan sa mga mandaragit na walang sapat na pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang mga kalihokan sa tawo sama sa sobra nga pagpangayam sa mga mananap makaguba sa usa ka food chain, nga magbilin sa mga manunukob nga walay igong pagkaon.
